For prestige property on Victoria’s Mornington Peninsula, I’d shortlist agencies based on three things: **demonstrated experience selling high-end homes, access to qualified local and international buyers, and knowledge of the specific coastal or hinterland market**\.

My strongest starting points are Peninsula Sotheby’s International Realty, Marshall White, Danckert Real Estate and RT Edgar, with Jellis Craig and McEwing & Partners also worth considering. They offer different strengths, from international exposure for exceptional homes to deep local knowledge and boutique service. ## Which agencies would I choose for different properties?

| Property type | First agencies I'd interview |
|--------|--------|
| Trophy home or exceptional waterfront estate | Peninsula Sotheby’s, Marshall White |
| Luxury home in Mount Martha or Mornington | Danckert, Marshall White |
| Portsea, Sorrento or Blairgowrie prestige home | RT Edgar, Peninsula Sotheby’s |
| Premium family home in Mount Eliza | Marshall White, McEwing & Partners |
| Coastal holiday home or lifestyle property | Jellis Craig, Peninsula Sotheby’s |
| Boutique service and local market knowledge | Danckert, McEwing & Partners |


These are recommendations based on agency positioning and publicly available information, not a definitive ranking of sale prices achieved. The individual agent and their recent comparable sales can matter more than the agency name.

## How to choose the right agent

Before signing an exclusive sales authority, I would ask each finalist for\:

- **Three comparable sales** from the last 12–18 months, ideally in the same suburb and price bracket.
- **A buyer-specific marketing plan\:** who they expect to buy the property and how they will reach those buyers.
- **Evidence of buyer demand\:** qualified buyers currently looking for similar homes, not just a large database.
- **A full campaign budget\:** commission, photography, styling, advertising and any premium international marketing.
- **A realistic price strategy\:** a reasoned price range and evidence behind it, rather than simply the highest appraisal.

For a prestige property, I would interview three agents and compare their actual sales evidence, marketing plans and communication style side by side.

**One question that would help me narrow this down\:** are you looking to *sell* a luxury property, *buy* one, or find an agency to manage a prestige holiday home? The best shortlist differs depending on your objective.

search_results.title: Why are rough sleepers dying a stone's throw from luxury waterfront houses in Victoria?
search_results.description: In the Mornington Peninsula, Victoria—an area known for its affluence and luxury homes—homelessness is claiming lives at an alarming rate. Over just six weeks, four rough sleepers have died, part of a larger tally of 11 deaths since December 2024. Despite the region having the second highest number of rough sleepers in the state, it suffers from a significant shortage of support services. Outreach workers Leonie and Pete, from the privately funded Southern Peninsula Community Support, report 111 people currently sleeping rough, struggling with mental illness, addiction, and a lack of affordable housing. The area's median rent has soared to $723 per week, exceeding even Melbourne's. Crisis accommodation is limited to a single facility with only seven units. The homeless — including families and working professionals — face years-long waitlists for public housing. Advocates stress that timely housing and mental health support could prevent many deaths. Launch Housing and local support workers urge the government to fund supportive housing. Although the Victorian government has pledged $2.1 million over four years for outreach, experts argue this is insufficient to address the complex, urgent crisis. Without systemic intervention, preventable deaths among the homeless will likely continue.

search_results.title: The Block 2026: Judges Darren Palmer, Marty Fox warn Mount Eliza contestants
search_results.description: In the upcoming 2026 season of The Block, set in Mount Eliza, judges Darren Palmer, Marty Fox, and Shaynna Blaze warn contestants that simply using expensive finishes won't be enough to attract buyers at the luxury end of the Mornington Peninsula market. Instead, the focus is on "quiet luxury"—refined, livable, and family-friendly homes with understated elegance and strong indoor-outdoor connections. Palmer, referencing Kim Kardashian’s minimalist home by Axel Vervoordt, emphasizes understanding the diverse buyer cohorts in the area, as failing to do so could hurt auction outcomes. With water views across Port Phillip Bay—a first for The Block—judges are stressing the importance of lifestyle appeal, full integration of outdoor living, and refined architectural detail. Fox warns that high-end buyers look for confidence and simplicity in design rather than overt expenditure, while Blaze notes the importance of understanding Mount Eliza’s unique lifestyle and discreet charm. The five contestant teams face a tough brief, and their ability to meet these lifestyle-driven expectations will begin to be tested with the first room reveals on Sunday.

search_results.description: A Hamptons-style home in Red Hill South, completed in 2024 and inspired by American architecture, has been listed with a price guide of $6.3 million to $6.7 million. The property, designed by Edward Baker and built with GEM Taylor Constructions, sits on a 6070sq m lot surrounded by lush botanical gardens and historic trees. Located within walking distance of top-rated wineries and restaurants, the home features high-end finishes, 3-meter ceilings, and a layout designed to offer privacy across different family wings. Interior highlights include a shaker-style kitchen with a marble benchtop, a wine cellar, and a moody marble-clad powder room. The open-plan living area features an open fireplace, while each bedroom has an ensuite, offering an exceptional family-friendly layout. Outdoor spaces feature French doors, a terrace, vine-draped pergola, established gardens, and a subterranean pool. The listing at 231 Red Hill Rd is handled by Stephen Baster of Marshall White Flinders.

These are recommendations based on agency positioning and publicly available information, not a definitive ranking of sale prices achieved. The individual agent and their recent comparable sales can matter more than the agency name.

## How to choose the right agent

Before signing an exclusive sales authority, I would ask each finalist for\:

- **Three comparable sales** from the last 12–18 months, ideally in the same suburb and price bracket.
- **A buyer-specific marketing plan\:** who they expect to buy the property and how they will reach those buyers.
- **Evidence of buyer demand\:** qualified buyers currently looking for similar homes, not just a large database.
- **A full campaign budget\:** commission, photography, styling, advertising and any premium international marketing.
- **A realistic price strategy\:** a reasoned price range and evidence behind it, rather than simply the highest appraisal.

For a prestige property, I would interview three agents and compare their actual sales evidence, marketing plans and communication style side by side.

**One question that would help me narrow this down\:** are you looking to *sell* a luxury property, *buy* one, or find an agency to manage a prestige holiday home? The best shortlist differs depending on your objective.
